lines.text: Hi! I'm Sofía. I'm a friend of Daniel.
Nice to meet you, Sofía. My name is Liam. Daniel is my neighbour.
Oh, nice! Are you from England, Liam?
No, I'm not. I'm from Australia. My family is in Perth.
Cool. My family is from Medellín, but my sister and I are in Bogotá now.
What's your job?
I'm a student. I'm in my second year of medicine. And you?
I'm an English teacher. My students are very nice.
Is your wife here tonight?
No, I'm single. But my friend Tom is here. His nickname is Tommo.
Ha! My nickname is Sofi. Daniel's nickname is Dani.
Well, Sofi, welcome to the party!

2.title: The Morning DJ
2.topic: Daily habits and telling people when things happen

lines.text: Oliver, you're a radio DJ, right? What time do you get up?
I get up at four o'clock in the morning. It's very early!
Wow! What do you have for breakfast?
I usually have coffee and toast. I take a taxi to the radio station.
When does your show start?
It starts at six and it finishes at ten.
What do you do after the show?
I have lunch with my team. Then I go home and sleep for an hour.
And what does your wife do?
She's a nurse. She works at night, so we have dinner together at seven.
Do you work at the weekend?
No, I don't. On Saturdays I always sleep late!

lines.text: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the Virgilio Barco Library.

3.title: Two Markets in Bogotá
3.topic: Pointing at things and comparing them
3.focus: Comparatives with short and long adjectives

lines.text: Hi, and welcome to City Tips, the podcast for visitors to Bogotá. I'm Jack.
Today I'm comparing two markets: Paloquemao and the Usaquén market.
Paloquemao is bigger than Usaquén. It has fruit, flowers, meat and fish.
It's also cheaper. A kilo of mangoes costs about four thousand pesos.
But Paloquemao is more crowded, especially early in the morning.
The Usaquén market is smaller and quieter. It's only on Sundays.
It's more expensive, but the crafts there are more beautiful.
Bags, hats and jewellery are lighter than fruit, so they're better for your suitcase!
So, which market is better? For food, Paloquemao. For presents, Usaquén.
See you next week!

Few students have aunts or uncles in another country. Only three.
All of the students have a mobile phone!
And no one in our class is married, of course. We're only fourteen!

15.title: A Message from Mum
15.topic: Future arrangements and passing messages on
15.focus: Messages with “tell” and “say” + requests with modals

lines.text: Hi, Nico, it's Mum. I'm running late. I'm still at the office.
Can you pick up your sister from school at four? Tell her to wait at the front door.
Your dad called me. He said that he's going to be home at seven.
Could you tell him that dinner is in the fridge?
Also, the dentist's office called. They said your appointment is on Tuesday, not Monday.
Please call them back and tell them that Tuesday is OK.
And Grandma is about to travel to Cali. Can you call her and say goodbye from me?
Don't forget to say thank you for the money!
OK, see you later. Love you!

16.title: Ten Years Later
16.topic: Comparing past and present, and looking ahead
16.focus: Comparing tenses: past simple, present simple, present perfect

lines.text: James? Is that you? I haven't seen you for ten years!
Carolina! Wow! You look great. Do you still live in Pereira?
No. I lived in Pereira until 2018. Now I live in Bogotá.
What do you do these days?
I'm a vet. I've worked in an animal hospital for three years. What about you?
Well, I moved back to London after school. I used to work in a bank, but I didn't like it.
So what do you do now?
Now I teach English online. I've had students from twelve countries so far.
That's great! Have you changed a lot?
A bit. I've grown a beard, and I've learned to cook!
Ha! Back then you only ate sandwiches.

16.title: Plans After School
16.topic: Comparing past and present, and looking ahead

lines.text: Welcome back to Young Voices. My guest today is Juan Pablo. He's finishing school next month. Juan Pablo, what are your plans?
First, I'm going to work in my uncle's restaurant for six months. I need to save some money.
And after that?
I want to study engineering at the National University. I hope to start in August.
Do you plan to live at home?
No, I've decided to share a flat with two friends. My mum isn't very happy about it!
What about travelling?
I'd like to visit Mexico one day. My best friend lives there now.
And in ten years?
I hope to have my own company. And I'm looking forward to having a dog!
